new_scholarship.description: The India Science and Research Fellowship (ISRF) is a Government of India scheme funded by the Department of Science and Technology and administered by the Indian National Science Academy. It lets researchers from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, the Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand undertake research for 3 to 6 months at premier Indian research laboratories and academic institutions. The 2025-26 call opened on 31 December 2025 and closed for proposals on 31 March 2026, awarding up to 80 fellowships, 10 per country. Up to 80 fellowships (10 per country) will be awarded annually under this scheme. The fellowship applications will be considered once a year by a Selection Committee.

new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be citizens or permanent residents of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, the Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka or Thailand, actively engaged in research at a university or research institution in their own country, below 45 years of age as on 31 March 2026, and hold a PhD, M.Tech, M.Sc or MBBS with 3-5 years of research or teaching experience. Applicants registered for a PhD in their home country may also apply. Each applicant may avail of the fellowship only once in five years, must hold a valid passport, and must not hold any Indian visa for temporary or permanent residency.

new_scholarship.description: The UGC Junior Research Fellowship and Research Associateship for Foreign Nationals lets students and teachers from developing countries of Asia, Africa and Latin America undertake advanced study and research leading to M.Phil or PhD, or postdoctoral research, in sciences, humanities and social sciences at Indian universities. Applications are invited through circulation to Indian embassies and Indian missions abroad, which screen applications locally before forwarding them to the UGC. The scheme is limited to 20 JRF and 7 RA slots, with JRF tenure of four years and RA tenure initially two years, extendable by a further two years.
new_scholarship.duration: JRF: four years. RA: initially two years, extendable by a further two years

new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Open to students and teachers from developing countries of Asia, Africa and Latin America. For JRF the upper age limit is 35 years for men and 45 years for women as on 1 July of the year of application, and the candidate must hold at least a high-class master's degree with a second-class bachelor's degree, or a second-class master's degree with a first-class bachelor's degree. For RA the age limit is 45 years for men and 50 years for women as on 1 July of the year of application, and the candidate must hold a doctorate degree with published research work and evidence of independent research. Foreign students from Asia, Africa and Latin America already studying in India who have completed their master's or doctoral degrees may apply through the university they propose to work with, with endorsement from their embassy in India.

new_scholarship.description: The Global Undergraduate Exchange Program, also known as the Global UGRAD Program, provides one semester scholarships to outstanding undergraduate students from around the world for non-degree full-time study in the United States combined with community service, professional development, and cultural enrichment. Public applications are accepted, and two organizations administer the programme on behalf of the Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs. Application deadlines vary by programme and region, and applicants apply through the U.S. Embassy or Fulbright Commission in their home country.

new_scholarship.description: Berea College provides a fully funded, no-loan degree to its students. Berea is the oldest continuously tuition-free college in the country and stopped charging tuition in 1892. Beginning in Fall 2027, Berea College will guarantee 100 per cent of tuition, housing, food, fees and supplies are covered, without loans, for all students, becoming the first college in the country to provide every enrolled student with a fully funded, no-loan degree. Berea's financial aid package combines Berea funding with federal and state grants, personal scholarships and other awards, and also funds Premier Perks including a laptop, a summer internship, professional clothing and conference attendance. Every student also works a campus job through the work college programme.

new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Berea College admits students who show strong academic accomplishments and come from families with limited financial resources. Admitted students average a 3.65 high school GPA and qualify for federal Pell Grants. While the college has a special commitment to students from Appalachia, it welcomes applicants from across the United States and from other countries. Most admitted families have an annual household income within the range of federal poverty guidelines. Berea is test-optional, letting applicants decide whether to submit ACT or SAT scores, and every applicant must submit a FAFSA to be considered for admission because of the financial eligibility requirement.
